value.name: decides to leave without rereading message
value.description: Asha chooses not to reread Rosa's message and prepares to leave the house with her bag.
evidence: she was not willing to start the trip there. She straightened, picked up the bag by its strap, and left the phone where it was.

value.name: retrieves phone and pockets it
value.description: At the front door, Asha goes back for the phone and slips it into her coat pocket without looking at the screen.
evidence: She crossed back to the counter, picked up the phone, and slid it into her coat pocket without turning the screen toward her; she already knew Rosa's message was the last thing on it, and she did not need to read it again to take it with her.

value.name: leaves the house
value.description: Asha locks the door, steps outside, and leaves the kitchen and its contents behind.
evidence: At the door she shifted the bag to her other shoulder, turned the lock, and stepped out, pulling it shut behind her so the latch caught on the first try.
The kitchen on the other side of the door held the laptop and the dishes and the chair where she had tied her shoes, and she left all of it where it was.

value.name: walks to car holding phone
value.description: Asha walks across the damp sidewalk toward her car, clutching the phone in her pocket as if it were fragile.
evidence: Outside, the sidewalk was damp from earlier rain, and Asha walked the half block to her car with her hand closed around the phone in her coat pocket, not pulling it out, just holding it the way she might hold a key she did not want to drop.

value.name: stops to read text message
value.description: When the phone buzzes, Asha stops on the curb and reads Rosa's text because it can be absorbed silently.
evidence: She had almost reached the driver's door when the phone buzzed once against her palm; she stopped on the curb and looked at it then, because a single buzz was a text and a text was something she could absorb without speaking.

value.name: learns form must be signed
value.description: Asha reads Rosa's message telling her the form is an MDS-discharge addendum that must be signed before Friday.
evidence: Rosa had sent only a line: the form was called an MDS-discharge addendum, and the social worker would need it signed before Friday.
